applicability: Any bridge, tube, pipe, corridor, gantry, cable run, conveyor, rail, or repeated connector assembly between two endpoints. Not limited to megacity builds.
core_rule: Compute one endpoint-to-endpoint path basis and apply it consistently to every repeated module, socket, collar, adapter, glass sleeve, rail, and support in the assembly.
required_steps: Compute source and target endpoints from actual attachment faces/sockets, not object origins unless the origin is the intended socket.
Calculate path vector, length, yaw, and pitch/3D basis from those endpoints.
For each ObjectID, map its native long axis to the path axis before placement.
Repeat modules along the normalized path vector with deliberate overlap/tolerance.
Use identical corrected path orientation for all modules in the same span unless a part-specific axis offset has been separately validated.
Add visible face sockets/adapters where the connector meets a building, hull, wall, or platform.

known_part_axis_notes.B_CON2_1: Validated in V10C/V12 as a path-aligned industrial connector; treat as connector/truss module and verify local axis in JSON if reused.
known_part_axis_notes.B_CON_L_1: Use same path-basis logic as the bridge connector family unless a new exported JSON proves a different native axis.
known_part_axis_notes.B_CON_R_1: Use same path-basis logic as the bridge connector family unless a new exported JSON proves a different native axis.
known_part_axis_notes.CORRIDOR_WATER: Previously produced visible axis mismatch as glass tube. Do not use as a bridge sleeve unless its native axis is explicitly aligned and then confirmed in exported JSON/screenshots.

failure_modes: Connector modules stair-step or stagger because centers follow a path but rotations remain generic.
Glass tube pieces point in a different direction than structural connectors.
Modules appear floating because endpoints were measured from object centers rather than attachment faces.
Long parts are stretched instead of repeated at real module scale.
